text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout v3.2.0 -> streaming-service (us-west) started: roll-id roll/2026-03-17-01. Target: 10% of traffic to canary group.

olivia (oncall): seeing alerts for increased 500s on /v1/stream and /v1/paging endpoints. Spikes started ~2m after canary.

maya (eng-runtime): confirming — telemetry shows handshake errors + cursor decode failures from SDK v3.2 clients.

rahul (sre): error pattern: `stream: handshake failed: invalid cursor encoding` repeated across hosts canary-*.usw1.

kevin (support): flagged by Support: 3 paying tenants (AcmeCorp, BetaMarket, ZenaLabs) reporting dropped streams and partial results. AcmeCorp on a call now.

lexi (customer-ops): pinged AcmeCorp with interim note, giving context that we are investigating and may back out canary. They flagged live transactions in progress.

maya (eng-runtime): quick log snippet: ```
ERR stream/handshake.go:92 invalid cursor: base64 decode failed: illegal padding
stack: runtime.go:45 -> kvcache.go:210
```

olivia (oncall): status check: do we have a compatibility shim? Can we flip a FF to stop canary?

chris (eng-platform): initiating emergency kill-switch: `ff.streaming_v3_canary = false` on prod. Also opening a rollback. Patching routing to exclude canary pool.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-17-01 — Canary streaming/paging regression. Priority: P1. Oncall: olivia.

maya (eng-runtime): quick mitigation: enable `allow_v2_cursor_compat` on canary hosts to accept older encoding, pushing now to all canary nodes. This is a short-lived shim.

rahul (sre): metric queries added: `sum(rate(stream.handshake_errors[1m])) by (host)` and `sum(rate(http.5xx[1m])) by (route)` — dashboards pinned to incident channel.

chris (eng-platform): running rollback: `releases rollback --id roll/2026-03-17-01 --scope streaming-service --confirm` -> started. Expected duration ~4m.

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued -> task id rb/2026-03-17-01. Progress: 0/12 canary hosts.

kevin (support): letting affected customers know we are rolling back; AcmeCorp paused their job, asked for ETA.

olivia (oncall): handoff note: I'll stay on for the rollback window. If rollback finishes and errors drop, we'll close incident then triage root cause.

maya (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: v3.2 upgraded cursor serialization to new binary layout; SDK release shipped with client-side encoding change. Server expects older base64-padded cursors for paging and streaming handshake. Canary exposed mismatch.

lexi (customer-ops): collecting impacted tenant list + recent request IDs from Support. Will post to incident doc.

rahul (sre): rb progress: 6/12 hosts rolled back, error rate dropping 35% on streaming route.

deploy-bot: Rollback job update -> rb/2026-03-17-01 progress 100% (12/12). Canary group removed from traffic.

olivia (oncall): verifying — monitoring shows streaming handshake errors back to baseline. 5xx rate normalized.

maya (eng-runtime): rolling forward a short-term compatibility patch to main fleet: `accept-legacy-cursor` toggled true; will still roll full fix in next patch.

kevin (support): notified AcmeCorp + BetaMarket + ZenaLabs that rollback completed and services restored. All said they will re-run jobs and report.

chris (eng-platform): opened follow-up PR to add automated canary rollback on handshake-failure rate > X threshold. Also scheduling postmortem.

olivia (oncall): incident summary for handoff: canary v3.2 introduced incompatible cursor encoding -> streaming/paging handshake errors -> customer impact (3 tenants) -> kill-switch + rollback restored service. Owning teams: eng-runtime (maya), eng-platform (chris), SRE (rahul), Support (kevin). Postmortem ETA: 48h.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-17-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem assigned to maya, chris.

maya (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) Revert SDK client encoding change or feature-flag it, 2) Add server-side defensive parsing for both cursor formats, 3) Add canary gating test that simulates mixed-client encodings.

olivia (oncall): closing loop here. If any regression after 1h, re-open incident. Thanks team :thumbsup:
